correctness.rationale: Under the specified plug-flow law the comparison is exactly U(t+h)>EU(t), where E=e^(κτ). The jth difference is a single phase-rotated cosine of positive amplitude c_j=b_j|e^(iω_jh)−E|, so the unique torus maximum is S=Σc_j. For a strict gain the excursion threshold (E−1)/ρ must be below S. If it is below S, an open set of phases satisfies it. The continuous-time Fourier averages vanish for every nonzero integer mode by integer-rational independence; the mean of the event is therefore its Haar volume, since for fixed first m−1 coordinates its boundary has at most two values of the last coordinate. This establishes existence for any initial phases above threshold, and impossibility at equality, reached phase or not. At ρ=ρ_c+ε, the deficit cap is δ=Sε/ρ; on centered torus coordinates, u_j=√(2c_j) sin(θ_j/2) gives S−Σc_jcosθ_j=|u|² exactly near the unique maximum. The inverse Jacobian tends to 2^(m/2)/√(∏c_j); integration over |u|²<δ and Haar normalization gives exactly the stated exponent and K_m. For m=1 this agrees with arccos(ρ_c/ρ)/π above threshold. Finally, each c_j≥b_j(E−1) with equality precisely at phase alignment, so a physically admissible above-threshold interval exists exactly when some tone is mismatched. Simultaneous alignment of two rationally independent positive frequencies forces h=0, with h=0 always safe. When all modes are aligned there is no admissible limit from above, as the record specifies.
residual_risks: Continuous-time, infinite-horizon equidistribution does not certify performance for finite or discretely sampled observation windows. Onset concerns fixed positive weights and nonresonant frequencies only.

evidence: Wang arXiv:1812.08004v1 §2.1 Lemma 2.5 restates the classical Morse lemma: at a nondegenerate critical point of index k there are local coordinates in which f=f(0)−Σ_{j≤k}x_j²+Σ_{j>k}x_j². The lemma itself imposes no equal-weight or restricted-dimension condition. Kronecker–Weyl gives time averages of bounded Riemann-integrable observables under the rational independence used here; its Fourier test is shown in RESULT.md, lines 46–50.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For a unique nondegenerate maximum of a smooth Morse observable f in dimension m, the superlevel deficit δ gives a coordinate ball of radius √δ. Put Q=−Hess f at the maximum in the original chart; Q is positive definite. Differentiating the normal form twice gives inverse coordinate Jacobian 2^(m/2)/√det Q there. Integrating a continuous density gives Euclidean ball volume times that Jacobian and the density at the maximum, to leading order. Here all critical phases of F have each angle 0 or π and diagonal Hessian entries ±c_j, hence all are nondegenerate; its unique maximum has Q=diag(c_j). With Haar density (2π)^(−m), this immediately covers the claimed prefactor and exponent for every stated m and unequal positive weights.

value.rationale: Matching parcels and avoiding a spurious increase are legitimate monitoring goals, and the formula is usable within the toy model. But the stated exact threshold is only the support bound for a phasor sum, the occupation law is the standard torus mean, and the onset is the ordinary dimension-over-two cap law with a diagonal Hessian. The unique all-amplitudes clock criterion is just simultaneous phase alignment. The record offers no independently nonroutine transport prediction, finite-horizon sampling bound, or other surviving mathematical consequence beyond these routine deductions. The judgment does not require field validation or a general theory for a narrow result; it rests on the fact that this exact invariant is mechanically implied.
residual_risks: An independently useful result for resonances or finite observation windows would be a different claim; none is proved here and no repair is made.
